data.one_liner: An adaptable floating bottom bar that reacts to scrolling and stays accessible.
data.what_it_does: It floats any widget above your content and automatically manages its visibility based on scroll notifications or imperative controllers. It provides adaptive sizing, custom motion, safe area handling, and keyboard avoidance.
use_when: You want a navigation or search bar that floats above scrollable content.
You need scroll-aware show and hide behavior without manual ScrollController plumbing.
You need an adaptable width layout that caps at a maximum width on tablets and desktop.
avoid_when: You require a traditional fixed-position bottom navigation bar integrated directly into the Scaffold.
Your scroll source does not bubble up ScrollNotification and cannot use reportScroll.
strengths: Notification-based scroll detection requires no complex controller plumbing.
Includes accessibility features such as non-interactive hidden states and proper touch targets.
Supports adaptive width configurations for wide screens and tablets.
weaknesses: Scrollables that do not emit ScrollNotification require manual reporting via controller methods.
Custom transition builders are strictly restricted to paint-only wrappers to maintain stable footprints.
data.minimal_example:
BottomBar(
  layout: const BottomBarLayout.adaptive(maxWidth: 420),
  body: BottomBarBodyPadding(
    padding: const EdgeInsets.only(top: 24),
    child: ListView.builder(
      padding: const EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal: 16),
      itemCount: 50,
      itemBuilder: (_, index) => ListTile(title: Text('Item $index')),
    ),
  ),
  child: const Padding(
    padding: EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal: 16, vertical: 14),
    child: Row(
      mainAxisAlignment: MainAxisAlignment.spaceBetween,
      children: [
        Icon(Icons.home_rounded),
        Text('Floating bar'),
        Icon(Icons.search_rounded),
      ],
    ),
  ),
)
